sources.entry: Mixio - Menu bar app with per-app & tab volume control, 10-band EQ with native style UI. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/RadixIV/Mixio) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]

summary.one_liner: Mixio is a free, GPL-3.0 macOS menu bar app that adds per-app volume control, per-tab volume for Safari and Chrome, and a 10-band equalizer to the native Sound menu.
summary.what_it_does: The app lives in the menu bar and opens a volume window styled to match native macOS menus. Each app currently playing sound gets its own slider, mute button, and icon that brings the app to the front. Safari and Chrome can be split into per-tab rows when enabled in Settings. The menu also lets you switch the output device and pick an EQ preset (Flat, Bass Boost, Treble Boost, Vocal, Loudness, or saved custom presets). A 10-band EQ runs from 32Hz to 16kHz with ±12dB faders and a frequency response visualizer. An optional custom on-screen display replaces the native volume HUD when volume keys are pressed, with steps of 1/16 (1/64 with Shift+Option).
use_cases: control volume of individual apps on macOS
lower one browser tab's audio without muting others
switch audio output device from the menu bar
replace the native volume HUD with a custom overlay
remember per-app volume levels across sessions
how_to_run: Download Mixio-x.y.z.dmg from the Releases page
Open the DMG and drag Mixio into Applications
Launch Mixio; grant System Audio Recording permission when prompted
Optionally grant Accessibility permission for the custom OSD
Build from source: git clone the repo, open Mixio.xcodeproj in Xcode (Sparkle resolves via Swift Package Manager), set your signing team, and build
stack: Sparkle (MIT, auto-updates via Swift Package Manager)
notable: Per-tab volume control for Safari and Chrome, not just per-app
Custom OSD is display-only and passes mouse clicks through to windows behind it
10-band EQ with a band visualizer overlaying real-time per-band levels
Signed with Developer ID and notarized, with in-app update checks
caveats: Per-app volume and EQ need System Audio Recording permission; the custom OSD needs Accessibility permission
Building from source requires Xcode with the macOS 26 SDK and your own signing team, because the entitlement is tied to the signing identity
Secure Input (such as password fields) blocks volume keys, so the native HUD appears instead
